newsitem.title: ITALY: Supporters visit Italy's Craxi in Tunisia.
newsitem.headline: Supporters visit Italy's Craxi in Tunisia.

text.p: Seventy die-hard Italian Socialists flew to Tunisia on Saturday on a pilgrimage to see their disgraced former leader, Bettino Craxi, who sought exile in the north African country after scandal forced his party to disband.
The former Socialist parliamentarians said they wanted to consult Craxi, a former prime minister and longtime Socialist leader, about their wish to relaunch the party.
"We are going to meet Bettino Craxi for two reasons: political and humanitarian," Margherita Boniver told reporters at Rome's Fiumicino airport before boarding a flight for Tunis.

"We are going to talk to (Craxi), a great European Socialist and a truly persecuted politician, about...the relaunching of a federation inspired by socialism, democracy and liberalism and to convey our solidarity to a very sick man," Boniver said.
The former premier lives in self-imposed exile in the resort of Hammamet, saying he is too ill with diabetes to return to Italy and that he would not get a fair hearing there anyway.
He moved to Tunisia in 1994 after being implicated in Italy's "Tangentopoli" (bribesville) scandals.

Craxi, 62, has been convicted in four corruption cases and sentenced to more than 25 years in jail but the sentences are subject to appeal. His lawyer has called for Craxi to be allowed back to Italy for medical treatment without fear of arrest.
Craxi's son, Bobo, was among the group of 70 people who flew to Tunis on two different flights from Rome. He ruled out the possibility that his father would enter politics again.
"A politician who was on the stage of public life for 15 years always has ways to make his voice heard without needing to the field," his son said.
